headline: Ho'nble Union Minister for Fisheries Animal Husbandry and Dairying & Panchayatiraj Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh launched Live Stock insurance portal
fullText:
Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying

Ho'nble Union Minister for Fisheries Animal Husbandry and Dairying & Panchayatiraj Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh launched Live Stock insurance portal

The digital platform aimed at transforming livestock insurance delivery across the country under the Livestock Insurance activity of National Livestock Mission (NLM)

Ho'nble Union MoS for Fisheries Animal Husbandry and Dairying & Panchayatiraj Prof S P Singh Baghel was also present on the occasion

28 SEP 2026 9:00PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Animal Husbandry & Dairying (DAHD), Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying, Government of India, today launched the Livestock Insurance Portal (https://rashtriyapashubima.dahd.gov.in), a comprehensive digital platform aimed at transforming livestock insurance delivery across the country under the Livestock Insurance activity of National Livestock Mission (NLM).

The Portal was launched by Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh, Hon'ble Union Minister of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying, in presence of Prof. S.P. Singh Baghel, Hon'ble Minister of State of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Shri Naresh Pal Gangwar, Secretary, Animal Husbandry and Dairyingand other senior officials of the Department, representatives of State Governments, insurance companies and sectoral stakeholders. Besides, more than 4,000 participants joined online.

While highlighting the contours of scheme, premium rates, contribution of the farmer & other aspects of scheme on the Livestock Insurance activity, Shri Naresh Pal Gangwar, Secretary (AHD) informed that more than 30 lakh animals have already been insured during the year.

Prof. S.P. Singh Baghel, Hon'ble Minister of State of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying expressed concern over uncertainty of agriculture and expressed hope that the livestock insurance portal will be a great relief to the farmers.

Speaking on the occasion, Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh, Hon'ble Union Minister of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying, highlighted that livestock serves as a critical source of income and livelihood for millions of rural households. He emphasized that timely and affordable insurance protection safeguards farmers against financial losses arising from mortality, disease outbreaks, accidents, natural calamities and other unforeseen risks. He stressed upon the measures for awareness programmes for the farmers, to provide them maximum benefit under the scheme. He also urged the Insurance Companies, State Governments and other stakeholders to give wider publicity to the scheme through their respective social media and IEC campaigns.

The newly launched Livestock Insurance Portal provides an end-to-end digital ecosystem for policy issuance, premium management, claim processing, beneficiary verification and real-time monitoring. The platform brings together farmers, State Governments, Insurance Companies and implementing agencies on a single transparent and technology-enabled interface.

The Portal is expected to:

simplify and expedite livestock insurance enrolment

enhance transparency and accountability in claim settlement

enable real-time tracking and monitoring of policies

improve accessibility and ease of doing business for farmers and insurance providers

strengthen data-driven decision-making for effective scheme implementation.

The initiative marks a significant step towards digital transformation in the livestock sector and supports the Government's vision of leveraging technology for farmer welfare and rural prosperity.

(Release ID: 2316242)
summaryText:
### OVERVIEW
The Department of Animal Husbandry & Dairying launched the Livestock Insurance Portal under the National Livestock Mission as a digital platform for nationwide livestock insurance delivery. The portal was launched by Union Minister of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh on 28 September 2026.

### KEY HIGHLIGHTS
- The Livestock Insurance Portal was launched at https://rashtriyapashubima.dahd.gov.in.
- The portal is part of the Livestock Insurance activity under the National Livestock Mission (NLM).
- The launch event was attended by Prof. S.P. Singh Baghel, Hon’ble Minister of State for Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying; Shri Naresh Pal Gangwar, Secretary, Animal Husbandry and Dairying; senior officials; State Government representatives; insurance companies; and sectoral stakeholders.

- Stakeholders were urged to provide wider publicity for the scheme through social media and IEC campaigns.

headline: Rashtriya Raksha University to Launch Second Batch of Masters in Financial and Economic Security
fullText:
Ministry of Home Affairs

Rashtriya Raksha University to Launch Second Batch of Masters in Financial and Economic Security

28 SEP 2026 8:44PM by PIB Mumbai

Mumbai, 28 September 2026

Rashtriya Raksha University (RRU), Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India, with the Indian Institute of Corporate Affairs (IICA), Ministry of Corporate Affairs, is set to launch the second batch of its Masters in Financial and Economic Security (MFES) program in November 2026. The program follows the successful completion of its first cohort, which comprised more than 40 professionals from diverse fields, including banking, law enforcement, investigation, academia, entrepreneurship and legal services.

Designed especially for working professionals, the one-year program is offered in a hybrid mode, enabling participants to continue their professional responsibilities while gaining specialised knowledge and practical skills. The program places strong emphasis on practical learning, hands-on training and exposure to contemporary challenges in financial and economic security.

Building Capacity for Emerging Financial and Economic Threats

Financial security and economic integrity are increasingly important in an interconnected global economy. The rapid evolution of financial technologies, digital assets and cross-border financial activities has also created new avenues for financial crime and economic disruption. There is therefore a growing need to build a specialised cadre of professionals capable of understanding, preventing and responding to emerging financial and economic crimes, thereby strengthening India’s economic resilience and contributing to international peace, stability and security.

Speaking at the National Stock Exchange (NSE), Mumbai, Mr. Sunil Kavishwar, Director, School of Criminal Law and Military Law, RRU highlighted the growing importance of safeguarding the integrity and resilience of financial systems. He noted that financial crimes are continuously evolving, moving beyond traditional forms into emerging areas such as virtual digital assets, terror financing, proliferation financing, and technology-enabled financial crimes. The increasing use of sophisticated technologies by criminal networks has further created new challenges for enforcement, regulatory and financial institutions.

Mr. Kavishwar highlighted that RRU has taken the lead in developing a global platform for capacity building, specialised training and knowledge exchange in the emerging field of financial and economic security. The University is working towards bringing together professionals, experts and institutions from across relevant domains to strengthen specialised understanding and practical capabilities in this area. He further highlighted that the MFES program brings together not only academicians but also experienced practitioners and working professionals who bring direct expertise from the field and will contribute to the program as faculty and resource persons.

Mr. Harshit Singh, Teaching Cum Research Officer, RRU spoke about the importance of developing a specialised professional cadre equipped to address emerging financial and economic security challenges. He emphasised that such trained professionals can contribute to strengthening India’s economic resilience, supporting sustainable national growth and enhancing the country’s contribution to global financial security and stability.

The program also aligns with the broader vision of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s Viksit Bharat @2047, by contributing to the development of skilled professionals capable of protecting financial systems, strengthening institutional capacity and responding effectively to emerging economic and security threats. As India’s economy becomes increasingly integrated with global financial systems, such specialised expertise can play an important role in supporting secure, resilient and sustainable growth.

The second cohort is open to national and international participants, providing an opportunity for professionals from different jurisdictions and sectors to learn and engage with contemporary issues of financial and economic security. The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) is also a Knowledge Partner in the program.

Interested professionals can register through the official Rashtriya Raksha University admission portal. The program is intended to provide participants with a multidisciplinary understanding of financial and economic security through academic instruction, practical exposure and interaction with experts from the field.

For further information and registration, visit the official Rashtriya Raksha University website.

PIB Mumbai | Sriyanka Chatterjee/Darshana Rane

headline: India showcases Forest and Landscape Restoration Initiatives at COFO 28, in Rome
fullText:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change

India showcases Forest and Landscape Restoration Initiatives at COFO 28, in Rome

International Cooperation must support Country-driven Implementation, Capacity Development, Technology Transfer and Measurable Outcomes on Ground: India

28 SEP 2026 8:21PM by PIB Delhi

India highlighted its significant achievement in forest and landscape restoration and reaffirmed its commitment to sustainable forest management, climate action and resilient forest landscapes at the Twenty-eighth Session of the FAO (Food and Agriculture Organization) Committee on Forestry (COFO 28), being held in Rome from 28th September to 2nd October 2026. Delivering its Statement during COFO 28, India welcomed FAO’s focus on Forest and Landscape Restoration, and emphasised that sustainable forest management provides an integrated framework for addressing restoration at the landscape level while responding to national circumstances and the needs of local communities.

India highlighted the consistent progress made in enhancing its forest resources. The country’s forest and tree cover stands at 82.74 million hectares, constituting 25.17% of its geographical area. The FAO Global Forest Resources Assessment 2025 ranks India 9th globally in forest area and 3rd in net annual forest area gain. Forests and trees also remain central to India’s climate commitments. India has created an additional carbon sink of 2.29 billion tonnes of CO₂ equivalent by 2021 and has enhanced its ambition to create an additional carbon sink of 3.5–4.0 billion tonnes of CO₂ equivalent by 2035, compared with 2005 levels.

The Statement further highlighted its commitment under the Bonn Challenge to restore 26 million hectares of degraded and deforested land by 2030, of which 21.76 million hectares have already been brought under restoration. Further, major landscape restoration initiatives being undertaken were showcased. Under the Aravalli Green Wall, approximately 6.45 million hectares of degraded land have been identified for restoration. In coastal landscapes, the MISHTI initiative is advancing mangrove restoration while strengthening climate resilience and supporting local livelihoods. India also highlighted that the number of Ramsar Sites in the country has reached 101.

The country also showcased Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam – Plant4Mother, a whole-of-government and whole-of-society initiative under which more than 3.5 billion saplings have been planted. India emphasised that international cooperation must move beyond global commitments to support country-driven implementation, capacity development, technology transfer and measurable outcomes on the ground. It underlined the need for effective and sustainable financing, particularly for developing countries, and encouraged FAO to strengthen support for accessing climate, biodiversity and blended finance and for developing long-term restoration programmes.

India also called for stronger coherence between FAO’s forestry work, the Global Forest Goals and other forest-related international processes, along with enhanced South-South and triangular cooperation for sharing knowledge, best practices and scalable solutions. The country reaffirmed its commitment to working with FAO and Member States in shaping the proposed UN Decade for Afforestation and Reforestation in line with Sustainable Forest Management, 2027–2036, with the objective of building a coherent continuum from restoration of degraded ecosystems to resilient, productive and inclusive forest landscapes.

headline: DoWR, RD & GR to implement Special Campaign 6 during 02-31 October, 2026
fullText:
Ministry of Jal Shakti

DoWR, RD & GR to implement Special Campaign 6 during 02-31 October, 2026

28 SEP 2026 8:15PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Water Resources, RD & GR, Ministry of Jal Shakti, has initiated preparations for Special Campaign 6, which will be implemented across the Department & its organisations from 2nd October to 31st October 2026, in line with the Guidelines of the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG). The Campaign will focus on institutionalizing cleanliness practices, improving space management and ensuring timely disposal of pending VIP/PMO etc. references in Government offices.

On 28.09.2026, Smt Archana Varma, Secretary, DoWR, RD & GR chaired a meeting with the Heads of Wings/Organisations of the Department regarding the preparatory phase of Special Campaign- 6. During the meeting, the preparedness of the Department and its organisations with regard to various activities/parameters under the campaign was reviewed. Secretary, DoWR instructed the officials to finalise the targets and to make all efforts to meet the targets by the end of Special Campaign- 6.

This year Campaign will accord special emphasis to scientific management of ewaste, with focus on effective collection, segregation and disposal of e-waste in accordance with the applicable rules and procedures. This will contribute towards environmentally responsible office management and sustainable workplace practices.

With Special Campaign 6, DoWR, RD &GR reaffirms its commitment in making cleanliness an integral part of daily office practices and ensuring the timely resolution of public matters in the spirit of transparency, efficiency and citizen-centric governance.

Further, Building on the achievements of the previous Special Campaign, DoWR, RD & GR has continued its efforts towards reducing pendency and ensuring timely disposal of various categories of references and public matters. The progress has been regularly monitored and updated on the SCDPM Portal of DARPG.

The achievements of the Department during the period from November, 2025 to August, 2026 have been as follows:

headline: India Energy Week 2027 Sets the Stage for Global Energy Dialogue in Kolkata
fullText:
Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas

India Energy Week 2027 Sets the Stage for Global Energy Dialogue in Kolkata

Hon’ble Minister for Petroleum and Natural Gas Shri Hardeep Singh Puri alongwith Hon’ble Chief Minister of West Bengal Shri Suvendu Adhikari formally announce Kolkata as the host city for India Energy Week 2027

Kolkata to host India Energy Week 2027

IEW 2027 theme: “Unlocking Innovation. Securing Energy. Shaping Tomorrow.”

75,000+ energy professionals and 700+ international exhibitors expected

IEW 2027 will be held from 28–31 January 2027 at the New Town Convention Centre, Kolkata, India

28 SEP 2026 8:11PM by PIB Delhi

As India’s energy demand continues to grow amid a rapidly shifting global energy landscape, the technologies, partnerships and strategic choices shaping the future of energy will be at the forefront of India Energy Week (IEW) 2027.

Making its debut in Kolkata from 28–31 January 2027 under the theme “Unlocking Innovation. Securing Energy. Shaping Tomorrow,” the fifth edition of IEW will serve as the first major global energy conclave of the year, bringing together policymakers, energy leaders, technology innovators, investors and industry stakeholders from across the world to explore pathways to strengthen global energy security and advance sustainability.

Held under the patronage of the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, India Energy Week has grown rapidly since its debut in Bengaluru in 2023, expanding in scale, international participation and the breadth of issues addressed. At the fourth edition in Goa in 2026, the event brought together 75,000+ energy professionals, 700+ exhibiting companies, participants from more than 120 countries and 6,500+ conference delegates, reflecting its preeminent position among global energy conclaves.

Union Minister for Petroleum and Natural Gas Shri Hardeep Singh Puri along with Chief Minister of West Bengal Shri Suvendu Adhikari formally announced Kolkata as the host city for India Energy Week 2027. Shri Adhikari thanked Shri Puri and the Petroleum & Natural Gas Ministry for bringing IEW 2027 to West Bengal. Shri Adhikari said a successful IEW 2027 would help attract new investment, expand existing projects and create employment opportunities in West Bengal.

The evolution of India Energy Week has taken place alongside India’s increasing importance to the global energy system. As the world’s fastest-growing major economy, India’s energy demand is expanding rapidly, while the country continues to balance energy security and affordability with its transition towards cleaner energy systems. India’s energy choices therefore have implications well beyond its borders, making the country a centre of the global energy conversation.

IEW 2027 will build on this context, focusing on the technologies, innovations and partnerships required to ensure energy security, affordability and sustainability for the globe, especially countries in the global South. The event will provide a meaningful platform for stakeholders from across the hydrocarbon and wider energy value chain to explore opportunities to scale innovation, strengthen energy security, improve efficiency and accelerate technology-led progress.

With energy security, affordability, technology, investment and sustainability increasingly interconnected, IEW 2027 promises to catalyse global efforts to find practical solutions to the challenges shaping the sector. The exhibition and conference programmes will showcase developments across oil and gas, LNG, refining and petrochemicals, hydrogen, biofuels, digitalisation and AI, alongside other emerging areas within the energy sector.

Kolkata: A New Chapter for India Energy Week

The move to Kolkata brings India Energy Week to eastern India for the first time, adding a new geographical dimension by providing a platform for businesses, institutions and energy stakeholders from the region to engage with international partners and participate in global conversations on energy.

The fifth edition is expected to bring together 75,000+ energy professionals and 700+ international exhibitors, alongside the decision-makers in the energy domain. The exhibition and conference programmes will provide opportunities to showcase technologies, forge partnerships and explore the strategic opportunities and challenges shaping the energy sector.

The international character of India Energy Week has also grown alongside its scale. Previous editions have brought together senior government leaders and energy executives from major energy-producing and consuming economies. 17 Ministers and Deputy Ministers from countries including UAE, Canada, Netherlands, Oman, Brunei, Myanmar, Tanzania participated in IEW 2026, along with International organisations such as the International Energy Forum, BIMSTEC and the Eurasian Economic Union.

Their participation reflected the increasingly interconnected nature of the energy conversation, as countries and companies navigate questions around energy security, investment, technology, transition and the changing global energy landscape.

About India Energy Week

India Energy Week is the country’s flagship global energy platform, bringing together government leaders, industry executives and innovators to accelerate progress toward a secure, sustainable and affordable energy future. As a neutral platform, India Energy Week drives investment, policy alignment and technological collaboration shaping the global energy landscape.

Held under the patronage of the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, India Energy Week 2027 is being organised by Federation of Indian Petroleum Industry (FIPI) with Informa Markets as Conference Organiser.

India Energy Week 2027 will take place from 28–31 January 2027 at the New Town Convention Centre, Kolkata, under the theme “Unlocking Innovation, Securing Energy, Shaping Tomorrow.”

For more information, visit: https://www.indiaenergyweek.com/

- Previous edition (IEW 2026 in Goa) recorded 6,500+ conference delegates, participation from 17 Ministers/Deputy Ministers (UAE, Canada, Netherlands, Oman, Brunei, Myanmar, Tanzania), and engagement with organisations such as the International Energy Forum, BIMSTEC, and the Eurasian Economic Union.  
- Organized by the Federation of Indian Petroleum Industry (FIPI) with Informa Markets as conference organiser, under the patronage of the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas.  
- First India Energy Week held in eastern India, intended to attract investment, expand existing projects, and generate employment opportunities in West Bengal.

headline: Union Education Minister holds bilateral meeting with French Minister for Higher Education in New Delhi
fullText:
Ministry of Education

Union Education Minister holds bilateral meeting with French Minister for Higher Education in New Delhi

India-France Year of Innovation 2026 provides a timely opportunity to deepen collaboration in education, research and innovation, says Shri Pralhad Joshi

The Ministers discuss academic mobility, institutional linkages, research collaboration and emerging areas of cooperation

French Minister H.E. Mr Philippe Baptiste is on a three-day visit to India from September 28 to 30, 2026

28 SEP 2026 7:54PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Education, Shri Pralhad Joshi, held a bilateral meeting with Minister for Higher Education, Research and Space of France, H.E. Philippe Baptiste, in New Delhi today. The two Ministers discussed ways to further strengthen cooperation between India and France in education, research, innovation, academic mobility and institutional partnerships.

Welcoming the French Minister and his delegation, Shri Pralhad Joshi highlighted the longstanding India-France partnership and emphasised that cooperation in education was an important pillar of the bilateral relationship. He said that the India-France Year of Innovation 2026 provided a timely opportunity to further deepen collaboration in education, research and innovation.

During the meeting, the two sides deliberated on the potential engagements in the field of higher education including strengthening institutional linkages; mobility of students, faculty and researchers; and expanding opportunities for collaborative academic programmes and exchanges. They also explored greater cooperation in life sciences, social sciences and humanities, with emphasis on institutional interaction, collaborative academic activities and research.

The Ministers exchanged views on further promoting knowledge partnerships between the two countries and discussed opportunities to build upon existing institutional collaborations and create new avenues for joint academic and research initiatives. French Higher Educational Institutions were invited to explore opening of branch campuses in India including in GIFT City, Gujarat and also at places where French companies were located and required technical human resources.

Acknowledging the importance of people to people ties, the two sides explored opportunities to strengthen language learning and teacher education, share academic expertise and promote technology-enabled learning. The discussions also covered ongoing revision of the Mutual Recognition of Qualifications (MRQ) Agreement between India and France, sharing experiences and best practices in digital education and leveraging technology to expand access to quality learning.

The meeting concluded with both sides reaffirming their commitment to further deepen India-France cooperation in higher education, innovation, language education and digital learning.

(Release ID: 2316187)

Union Minister for Education Shri Pralhad Joshi held a bilateral meeting with French Minister for Higher Education, Research and Space H.E. Philippe Baptiste in New Delhi on 28 September 2026 to advance India‑France cooperation in education, research, innovation, academic mobility and institutional partnerships, underscoring the India‑France Year of Innovation 2026 as a catalyst for deeper collaboration.

### KEY HIGHLIGHTS
- French Minister H.E. Philippe Baptiste visited India from 28 September to 30 September 2026.  
- Discussion focused on strengthening institutional linkages, student/faculty/researcher mobility, and expanding collaborative academic programmes and exchanges.  
- Explored greater cooperation in life sciences, social sciences and humanities, emphasizing institutional interaction and joint research activities.  
- French higher‑education institutions invited to consider opening branch campuses in India, notably in GIFT City, Gujarat, and near French company locations requiring technical talent.  
- Opportunities to strengthen language learning, teacher education, sharing of academic expertise, and promotion of technology‑enabled learning were examined.  
- Ongoing revision of the Mutual Recognition of Qualifications (MRQ) Agreement between India and France was reviewed, with exchange of best practices in digital education.  
- Both sides committed to deepening cooperation in higher education, innovation, language education and digital learning.

headline: Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah inaugurates the Conference on ‘PRAHAAR - CT Policy and Strategy’ in New Delhi
fullText:
Ministry of Home Affairs

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah inaugurates the Conference on ‘PRAHAAR - CT Policy and Strategy’ in New Delhi

The Conference deliberated upon the seven pillars of PRAHAAR including Prevention, Response, Aggregating Internal Capacities, Human Rights, Attenuating Conditions for Terrorism, Aligning International Efforts and Recovery & Resilience through a whole-of-society approach

Under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the Government of India has adopted a 'zero-tolerance' policy against all forms and manifestations of terrorism

Consistent efforts are required to strengthen the 'PRAHAAR' strategy through a continuous analysis of terror incidents and establishing a strong and concrete 'PRAHAAR' mechanism for the next 10 years

Union Home Minister impressed upon adopting a proactive approach towards every aspect of the 'PRAHAAR' initiative to ensure its implementation down to the police station level

There is a need to institutionalize an automated counter-terrorism response at every level of the 'PRAHAAR' framework

Better coordination among all stakeholders is essential to prevent any delays in action and to ensure that every pillar of 'PRAHAAR' is result-oriented

Union Home Minister launched a new Extradition Portal, which will synergise and expedite the efforts to bring back fugitives from abroad

From 2019 to 2026, the Modi Govt. successfully brought back 288 fugitive criminals to India from 36 countries

As a result of better coordination among agencies, more than 40 modules of Shahzad Bhatti network involved in cross-border smuggling of weapons, explosives and narcotics were busted, more than 100 FIRs were registered and 350 individuals were arrested across 15 states

At the same time, Modi Govt. declared Shahzad Bhatti network a terrorist organisation under UAPA

State police forces should establish dedicated teams to work intandem withcentral agencies to bring back fugitives from abroad

28 SEP 2026 6:57PM by PIB Delhi

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah inaugurated the Conference on ‘PRAHAAR - CT Policy and Strategy’ today in New Delhi. The Conference deliberated upon the seven pillars of PRAHAAR including Prevention, Response, Aggregating Internal Capacities, Human Rights, Attenuating Conditions for Terrorism, Aligning International Efforts and Recovery &Resilience through a whole-of-society approach. The Conference was attended by Union Home Secretary, Foreign Secretary, Heads of CAPFs/CPOs, DGsP of 15 States, ATS Chiefs of all the States/UTs in person while other State DGsP and cutting-edge police officers joined the Conference virtually.

In his address, Union Home Minister said that under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the Government of India has adopted a 'zero-tolerance' policy against all forms and manifestations of terrorism.He also stressed on the need for consistent efforts to strengthen and improvise the PRAHAAR strategy through a continuous analysis of terror incidents and establishing a strong and concrete PRAHAAR mechanism for the next 10 years. Focussing on percolation of the tenets of PRAHAAR up to the Thana level, he impressed upon adopting a proactive approach towards every aspect of the PRAHAAR initiative. Mentioning various steps undertaken for mitigating terrorist threats, he advocated institutionalising an automated counter terrorism response at every level of the framework. Impressing upon the necessity of result-oriented approach towards each pillar of PRAHAAR, he called for coordination among the stakeholders to prevent any delay in action. Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah said, from 2019 to 2026, the Modi Govt. successfully brought back 288 fugitive criminals to India from 36 countries. As a result of better coordination among agencies, more than 40 modules of Shahzad Bhatti network involved in cross-border smuggling of weapons, explosives and narcotics were busted, more than 100 FIRs were registered and 350 individuals were arrested across 15 states. He said, at the same time, Modi Govt. declared Shahzad Bhatti network a terrorist organisation under UAPA.

Union Home Minister also launched a new Extradition Portal, which will synergise and expedite the efforts to bring back fugitives from abroad. He exhorted the State Police Forces to establish dedicated teams for working in tandem with the Central agencies to bring back fugitives from abroad.

(Release ID: 2316153)

Read this release in:
summaryText:
### OVERVIEW
Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah inaugurated the Conference on ‘PRAHAAR - CT Policy and Strategy’ in New Delhi, emphasizing India's zero-tolerance policy against terrorism, the need to strengthen the seven-pillar PRAHAAR strategy for the next decade, and the launch of a new Extradition Portal to facilitate the return of fugitive criminals.

### KEY HIGHLIGHTS
- Conference deliberated on seven pillars of PRAHAAR: Prevention, Response, Aggregating Internal Capacities, Human Rights, Attenuating Conditions for Terrorism, Aligning International Efforts, and Recovery & Resilience through a whole-of-society approach.  
- Under Prime Minister Narendra Modi, the Government of India has adopted a 'zero-tolerance' policy against all forms and manifestations of terrorism.  
- The PRAHAAR strategy must be strengthened through continuous analysis of terror incidents and a concrete mechanism for the next 10 years, with percolation down to the police station (Thana) level.  
- Institutionalizing an automated counter-terrorism response at every level of the PRAHAAR framework was stressed to ensure proactive implementation.  
- Better coordination among all stakeholders is essential to prevent delays and ensure each pillar of PRAHAAR is result-oriented.  
- A new Extradition Portal was launched to synergise and expedite efforts to bring back fugitives from abroad.  
- From 2019 to 2026, the Modi Government successfully brought back 288 fugitive criminals to India from 36 countries.  
- Over 40 modules of the Shahzad Bhatti network, involved in cross-border smuggling of weapons, explosives, and narcotics, were busted, with more than 100 FIRs registered and 350 individuals arrested across 15 states.  
- The Shahzad Bhatti network was declared a terrorist organisation under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA).  
- State police forces should establish dedicated teams to work in tandem with central agencies to bring back fugitives from abroad.

headline: Union Health Minister Shri J.P. Nadda Reviews Progress of Lady Hardinge Medical College and its Associated Hospitals
fullText:
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare

Union Health Minister Shri J.P. Nadda Reviews Progress of Lady Hardinge Medical College and its Associated Hospitals

Shri Nadda Emphasises Long-Term Vision, Quality and Timely Execution for Upcoming Infrastructural Projects

Union Health Minister visits Advanced Simulation-Based Training and Neonatal Care Facilities at LHMC and KSCH; Highlights the role of simulation-based training and advanced neonatal care in strengthening patient safety and clinical outcomes

28 SEP 2026 6:50PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Health and Family Welfare Shri J.P. Nadda reviewed the progress of Lady Hardinge Medical College (LHMC) and its associated hospitals, Smt. Sucheta Kriplani Hospital (SSKH) and Kalawati Saran Children’s Hospital (KSCH), with a focus on strengthening healthcare infrastructure, specialised clinical services, medical education, research and patient care.

During the review meeting, the Minister was apprised of the ongoing augmentation of Kalawati Saran Children’s Hospital. The project envisages increasing the hospital’s total bed capacity from 394 to 894 beds, ICU capacity from 40 to 200 beds and the number of Operation Theatres from 4 to 12. Construction work on the KSCH campus is underway and is aimed at strengthening tertiary and super-speciality paediatric care, while also expanding capacity for undergraduate, postgraduate and super-speciality medical education and training.

Addressing the review meeting, Shri Nadda emphasised that the ongoing and upcoming projects at LHMC and its associated hospitals must be planned with a patient-centric and future-oriented approach, keeping evolving medical requirements at the core. He stressed that planning and design should draw upon the expertise and best practices of leading institutions in the relevant fields, while ensuring high quality of construction and strict monitoring of project timelines. He called for timely escalation of issues requiring approvals and clearances to the Ministry and emphasised that infrastructure expansion and recruitment of nurses, doctors and other healthcare professionals must progress concurrently.

Looking ahead, he called for a comprehensive master plan with a long-term institutional vision, combining immediate priorities with phased development and a forward-looking perspective for the coming decades. He also encouraged exploring private-sector expertise and partnerships, wherever appropriate, in planning and implementing major projects, while ensuring that quality, efficiency and patient care remain central to all such initiatives.

As part of the visit, the Union Health Minister visited the state-of-the-art Skill Lab at Lady Hardinge Medical College, a comprehensive multidisciplinary simulation-based training facility that provides hands-on and competency-based learning in a safe and controlled environment. The facility has dedicated simulation areas for ICU, surgical skills, simulated OT, Obstetrics OT, NICU, trauma, ENT and ophthalmology, along with briefing and debriefing areas and task trainers for procedural skills.

The Skill Lab provides an integrated platform for undergraduate and postgraduate training, procedural skills development, faculty development, multidisciplinary team training and competency-based assessment. Simulation-based learning, deliberate practice and structured feedback at the facility support the development of clinical and surgical proficiency, decision-making, teamwork, communication and crisis-resource management, while contributing to enhanced patient safety.

The Minister also visited the recently functional Augmented Level III-B Neonatal Care Centre at Kalawati Saran Children’s Hospital and reviewed the advanced facilities available for newborn care.

The Department of Neonatology has 80 intensive care beds and caters to more than 10,000 deliveries and 2,500 NICU admissions annually, with overall survival exceeding 93 per cent. The neonatal care facility provides advanced services including high-frequency oscillatory ventilation (HFOV), inhaled nitric oxide therapy, therapeutic hypothermia, advanced monitoring and comprehensive respiratory support.

The recently functional NICU-B comprises 7 NICU beds, 8 HDU beds, 15 Kangaroo Mother Care (KMC) beds and 12 mothers’ cots, with emphasis on family-integrated care, kangaroo mother care and breastfeeding support.

The review and visit underscored the continued efforts of LHMC and its associated hospitals to strengthen advanced patient care, specialised paediatric and neonatal services, medical education, simulation-based training and research, alongside the ongoing expansion and modernisation of healthcare infrastructure.

Shri Sunil Kumar Barnwal, CEO, National Health Authority (NHA); Dr. L.G. Krishna, DGHS; Smt. G.S. Chitra, Joint Secretary, Ministry of Health and Family welfare and Dr. Himani Ahluwalia, Director, Lady Hardinge Medical College (LHMC); Dr. Arvind Kumar, Medical Superintendent, LHMC; Dr. Vikram Dutta, Medical Superintendent, LHMC and Dr. Sujata Gautam, Principal, LHMC were present at the review meeting.

headline: District Awareness Programme on Labour Codes Held at Regional Labour Institute, Faridabad as part of Shram Samvad Initiative
fullText:
Ministry of Labour & Employment

District Awareness Programme on Labour Codes Held at Regional Labour Institute, Faridabad as part of Shram Samvad Initiative

28 SEP 2026 6:46PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Labour and Employment organised a District Awareness Programme, as part of its “Shram Samvad” Awareness Campaign, at the Regional Labour Institute, Faridabad today. The Shram Samvad Campaign, launched with effect from today, is aimed at creating awareness among stakeholders regarding the recently introduced Labour Codes and the key provisions and compliances applicable thereunder. Industrial clusters across 316 districts in all 36 States and Union Territories will be covered over the next 90 days under this initiative.

The programme at Faridabad witnessed enthusiastic participation from around 75 participants including employers, state authorities, advocates and other representatives and stakeholders from the labour and employment ecosystem. It was structured into five informative sessions, covering the major provisions of the new Labour Codes, employer compliances, and key social security schemes of the Government of India.

The inaugural address was given by Ms. Mridula Ghai, ACC, Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO), and Ms. Aprajita Jaggi, ACC, EPFO. Mr. Ashish Wig, Member, Central Board of Trustees & Chair HR and IR Committee, PHDCCI, also addressed the gathering on this occasion.

The first technical session was conducted by Mr. Minhaz Ahmed, Director, Ministry of Labour and Employment. He provided an overview of the new Labour Codes, explaining their objectives and highlighting the major provisions and changes introduced under the new legislative framework. The session focused on providing participants with a broad understanding of the Labour Codes and their significance for employees and employers.

The second session was conducted by Mr. Hemant Tirkey, Labour Welfare Commissioner, who elaborated upon the major compliances to be undertaken by employers under the Labour Codes. The session provided practical insights into the responsibilities and statutory requirements applicable to employers and helped participants understand the compliance framework under the new Codes.

The third session focused on the Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maandhan (PM-SYM) Scheme and was conducted by Mr. Sunil Gautam, Assistant Welfare Commissioner. The participants were apprised of the salient features of the scheme and its role in extending social security benefits to eligible unorganised workers.

The fourth session was dedicated to the Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana (PMVBRY) and was conducted by Mr. Pranit Joshi, Regional Provident Fund Commissioner-I. The session provided participants with an overview of the scheme, its objectives and the relevant provisions and benefits associated with it.

The programme concluded with an interactive Question and Answer session, wherein participants actively engaged with the speakers and raised queries relating to the implementation and compliance requirements under the new Labour Codes. The session provided an opportunity for participants to seek clarifications on various aspects of the Codes and related labour welfare schemes.

The programme served as an important platform for awareness generation and stakeholder engagement, facilitating a better understanding of the new Labour Codes, employer compliances and Government initiatives aimed at strengthening labour welfare and social security.

Rini Choudhury/Anjelina Alexander

(Release ID: 2316147)
